research.title: Robustness of Semantic Segmentation Under Camera Degradation
bullets: Designed controlled experiments varying blur, sensor noise, and compression to assess segmentation robustness while holding training data and model configurations fixed.
Analyzed classwise overlap scores and boundary errors to distinguish degradation sensitivity in small objects from failures across larger background regions.

research.title: Illumination Shift in Visual Surface Defect Detection
bullets: Designed comparisons of illumination normalization and color augmentation for surface defect detection, using specimen separated splits to limit visual leakage.
Analyzed precision recall behavior across lighting conditions and inspected false detections to characterize confusion between surface defects, shadows, and specular reflections.

publications.title: Evaluating Illumination Normalization and Color Augmentation for Visual Surface Defect Detection

work.title: Image Ingestion Validation and Preprocessing
bullets: Implemented image validation and resizing routines within an existing ingestion service, handling unsupported formats and malformed files through established error reporting paths.
Added regression tests for orientation handling and color conversion, and investigated preprocessing failures using service logs and representative image fixtures.

projects.title: Comparative Evaluation of Stereo Matching Methods
bullets: Implemented block matching and semiglobal matching for rectified stereo images, comparing disparity estimates under consistent preprocessing and disparity search ranges.
Evaluated disparity errors in occluded and low texture regions, examining how matching window size and smoothness penalties affected reconstruction artifacts.

projects.title: Transfer Learning for Fine Grained Image Classification
bullets: Implemented frozen feature extraction and partial fine tuning with a pretrained convolutional network, maintaining identical data splits and augmentation settings.
Compared classification errors and training behavior across adaptation strategies, using confusion matrices to inspect mistakes between visually similar object categories.
